The Federal Reserve (Fed) influences borrowing costs, savings returns, and overall financial conditions across the [economy](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/economic-recovery-status.html). At its [June 17 meeting](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-interest-rate.html), the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held its target federal funds interest rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range, a decision investors broadly expected. The decision kept the Fed in a patient but [inflation](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/investing-insights/how-does-inflation-affect-investments.html)-focused policy stance. Shelter costs increased 3.4% over the year, but slower home-price and rent growth may still help cool official inflation readings over time.[1](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_7424). The unemployment rate stood at 4.3% in May, and weekly initial jobless claims remained low at 228,000 in the week ending June 5.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_621e). The Fed recently announced it would reduce regular purchases, and its bond holdings now stand near $6.7 trillion after peaking near $9 trillion in 2022.[3](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_d324).
